question: The EU has increased its efforts to become less dependent on energy supplies from countries outside the EU. However, the EU must not only reduce its dependence on fossil fuels, but must also ensure the energy industry is resilient and self-sufficient across the board. The aim of the Net Zero Industry Act is for 40 % of clean technologies to be manufactured within the EU itself by 2030.

In terms of manufacturing inverters for solar panels, China is currently the clear leader in the EU market and has significantly built up its market share in the past ten years, while EU suppliers have largely been driven out.

Not only are Chinese products often produced under questionable conditions, but the possibility of these companies accessing the systems remotely also represents a serious danger to the EU’s energy security, which could even lead to a widespread blackout in a well-developed solar energy grid.
Is the Commission planning to introduce EU-wide rules for photovoltaic products to make it easier for SMEs based in the EU to supply the entire EU market?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (8.4.2024) As part of the Green Deal Industrial Plan1, the Commission is committed to strengthening the resilience and competitiveness of the EU’s solar Photovoltaic (PV) industry, making energy system safer and more sustainable across the EU.

The Commission is aware of the challenges European PV industry faces due to the very low prices of imported panels and it makes considerable efforts to support it. Amongst the measures, on 6 February 2024, a provisional political agreement was reached on the Net-Zero Industry Act2 (NZIA), part of the Green Deal Industrial Plan.

This agreement is a significant stride towards reinforcing EU manufacturing capabilities for clean technologies, including solar PV. The Act will enhance the EU industry’s competitiveness and resilience, including for small and medium enterprises (SMEs).

SMEs benefit from a number of provisions, such as the priority access to innovative net-zero regulatory sandboxes - which are referred also under action 7 of the SME relief package3 - particular administrative and operational assistance by Member States for net-zero technology manufacturing projects, and the possibility to participate in the Net-Zero Industry Group under the Net-Zero Europe Platform.
Moreover, SMEs are welcome to become members of the European solar PV industry alliance that groups the stakeholders of the European solar sector and makes their voices heard.
